newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Supreme Court sides with Sara Lee on trademark.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Supreme Court sides with Sara Lee on trademark.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by Kayser-Roth Corp in a trademark dispute with Sara Lee Corp over pantyhose products.

The court let stand a federal appeals court ruling that Kayser-Roth's use of the trademark "Leg Looks" on a line of its products infringed Sara Lee's "L'eggs" trademark. The appeals court barred Kayser-Roth from any future infringement.

Kayser-Roth, owned by Synchro SA de CV, is Sara Lee's only nationwide competitor. In the past 20 years the two firms have spent hundreds of millions of dollars to advertise their pantyhose and other ladies' hosiery products, the appeals court said.
Sara Lee sued in 1992, right after Kayser-Roth introduced a new line of pantyhose. Sara Lee charged the name "Leg Looks" infringed on its "L'eggs" product.

A federal judge ruled for Kayser-Roth, saying use of "Leg Looks" for the pantyhose sold in food, drug and mass merchandising outlets was not trademark infringement. But the appeals court disagreed and ruled for Sara Lee.
Kayser-Roth asked the Supreme Court to hear the case, but the justices sided with Sara Lee and denied the appeal without any comment or dissent.
